description: turbo-tasks-fs: DiskFileSystem::write keeps the persisted file content in a cell of its own task instead of a separate FileContent::persist task. The task that takes the effects reads each write task's effect cell, so a warm build's prefetch restores the write tasks with their cells in one parallel batch; before, each effect's capture restored its content task with an untracked read, one at a time on the thread taking the effects. Test: a second session restored from the persistent cache applies the writes it does not run again, rewriting files deleted between the sessions. Not taken: a warm build with nothing changed spends 1.2 to 1.3s less in run-turbopack but longer starting the page-data workers, with about 1 GiB more memory at its peak (cache-drift.md)
